hypothesis: The fleet's fresh-write durability class (fresh temp + fsync/sync_all + rename + stat) is subject to a TIME-VARYING, FLEET-SYNCHRONIZED storage-layer regime (the fleet's historical ~0.3ms vs 40-450ms flapping, spawned dual-class probe standard): characterize whether the regime is host-level, per-VM, or fleet-wide correlated; whether it correlates with the product's own write bursts or is idle-correlated; and deliver a regime calendar + measurement-trustworthiness advisory. Infra characterization lane: NO product change.
approach: Longitudinal dual-class probe series on 3 fresh VMs (a=16c/32GB dense+burst, b=4c/8GB dense+burst, c=4c/8GB QUIET ambient control) + a light probe on the orchestrator host (different infra class). 30s rich samples (fresh4k/64k/256k+sync_all+rename, fresh4k+fdatasync+rename, fresh+rename-no-fsync control, append+fsync, repeat-fsync 4KB, cached-read control, O_DIRECT 4KB control) with per-sample guest counters (/proc/stat incl steal, meminfo Dirty/Writeback, vmstat, PSI, root-cgroup io.stat/io.psi/cpu.stat, raw diskstats); 0.5s dense isolated-flush stream on a+b (stall structure/periodicity); 100-op back-to-back burst + 6-op recovery tail every 10min on a+b only (self-induction test); flock-guarded detached probes, raw JSONL, no transcription. 6h duration 2026-09-26T23:45Z -> 2026-09-27T05:45Z.

regime_calendar_advisory: FINAL ADVISORY v1.0 (supersedes v0.9 broadcast): (1) The regime is OP-LEVEL BIMODAL — p50-of-small-n probes are a NECESSARY but INSUFFICIENT gate (0-5 degraded 30s-p50s across ~400 samples/VM while 3.6-6% of isolated ops stalled 15ms-19.4s; pearson on p50 series ~0 while stall-rate pearson 0.75-0.87). Gate on: >=40 ISOLATED fresh+sync_all+rename ops at >=0.3s spacing (0.5s fine, ~20-25s) + >=20 repeat-fsync; HEALTHY = stall-rate(>15ms) <=2% AND max <=50ms AND baseline p50 <=2x host known-good; MARGINAL (2-5% / max 50-100ms / baseline >2x) = re-probe in 2-5min; DEGRADED (>5% sustained or max >100ms) = no timing legs, re-probe ~every 5min. (2) NEVER judge the regime with back-to-back probe streams (they AMORTIZE: 100-op bursts ran at 0.18-4.07ms p50 with 0-4 stalls even inside incident windows) — isolated ops only; bursts mask exactly the trap class. (3) Per-host baselines diverge (0.7-2.5ms fast/slow states, ~5ms lifted) — thresholds are HOST-RELATIVE; never compare absolute ms across hosts; flag >2x baseline lifts even at low stall rate. (4) The incident process is CLUSTERED not cyclic: chronic multi-minute windows and ~15-25min band cadence alternate with fully-quiet hour-plus stretches; mid-leg re-probes for any leg >5min; label every timing leg with its regime state. (5) Both probe classes remain required (class divergence observed in BOTH directions across this series). (6) For the PRODUCT: single durability writes (session open, spawn admission, config persist, sidecar cert) pay per-op trap costs 30-50ms typical, tail to 19.4s; write storms (resume storms, concurrent appends) amortize (~0.2-3.5ms/op) — attribution of absolute walls must use the leg-time regime label, and same-VM interleaved ABBA arms pay symmetric stall rates (paired deltas survive MARGINAL windows).
root_cause_hypothesis: ROOT-CAUSE (provisional, evidence-based): a fleet-shared storage-backend flush-path layer serves sandbox-VM durability writes; it (i) runs a per-request TRAP mechanism whose victims are in-flight FLUSH requests (fsync AND fdatasync stall; no-fsync rename, O_DIRECT writes and cached reads are untouched through the same windows; back-to-back flush streams AMORTIZE through it at ~0.2-3.5ms/op), (ii) fires SYNCHRONIZED across independent VMs (matched trap instants within 0-8s across a/b/c: 19s twin pairs at 00:33 and 02:28, quad 1.2-2.1s at 01:38, five 100-200ms bands) => the cause is upstream of every VM (the sandbox-fleet shared storage/host layer), not per-VM or product-induced; (iii) produces magnitudes 100ms-19.4s with no observed ceiling, hitting 1-2 requests per VM per incident; (iv) arrives CLUSTERED, NOT CYCLIC (chronic 10-min window, band cadence ~15-25min, then a fully-quiet 1h+ stretch; the 2 extreme twins are sporadic — the fixed-115min-cycle prediction was REFUTED by a live covered window with zero events); (v) coexists with an independent per-host BASELINE STATE MACHINE (fast ~0.7-1.1ms / slow ~2.2-2.5ms / lifted ~5ms states switching on minutes-to-hours scales, unsynchronized across hosts — the fast/slow/lifted states are per-host, NOT the trap mechanism). Guest counters show NO cause (steal ~0.2%, Dirty 32-112KB, loadavg ~0) and the orchestrator host (different infra) is UNTOUCHED through every incident. Most economical model consistent with all evidence: backend-side flush-batching/commit-cycle machinery (e.g., periodic maintenance/GC/rebalance of a shared storage layer, possibly coalescing FLUSH/FUA commands across tenants) that intermittently traps in-flight flush requests; the fleet-synchronization proves shared infrastructure, the per-request structure proves the trap not a freeze, the burst-amortization proves pipeline batching, and the unbounded magnitudes prove a non-local (remote/queued) dependency.

burst_self_induction_verdict.final: 31 bursts per VM (3,100 burst ops each arm): burst p50 range a 0.25-4.07ms / b 0.18-1.49ms, total stalls 7/3100 (a) and 1/3100 (b) — back-to-back streams AMORTIZE in every baseline state and every incident window; ambient stalls continued at their own cadence through every burst; post-burst tails mirror ambient state. VERDICT: the regime is NEVER product/self-induced; it is an ambient fleet-storage property. Product implication: single durability writes pay the trap costs; write storms amortize (per-op ~0.2-4ms even in incident windows).
